title: Unified Strong-Field Dynamics Simulations from Atoms to Heterostructures
abstract: We present \textsc{TDSE-Z}, a high-performance open-source framework for strong-field quantum dynamics in atomic, molecular, and semiconductor effective-mass systems. The core engine implements a weak-form Galerkin discretisation of the Hermitian BenDaniel-Duke operator, $\hat{T}_{\mathrm{BDD}} = -\frac{1}{2}\nabla\cdot(m^{-1}(\mathbf{r})\nabla)$, on geometry-adapted B-spline meshes, supporting arbitrary potentials and customisable laser configurations in one to three dimensions. We validate the static position-dependent-mass (PDM) eigensolver through two stringent benchmarks: a comparison to the analytical Quesne PDM model and a $\text{GaAs/Al}_{0.3}\text{Ga}_{0.7}\text{As}$ double quantum well, where the exponential decay of computed tunnel splittings follows Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) theory at the sub-percent level. We further demonstrate the time-propagation engine on constant-mass systems, accurately reproducing high-harmonic generation (HHG) spectra in atomic benchmarks and confirming the importance of dimensionality in fully capturing the strong light-matter interaction. Our implementation demonstrates robust strong-scaling efficiency, maintaining performance across hundreds of CPU cores. While the static eigensolver currently supports optional GPU offloading, the time-propagation engine is CPU-optimised, providing a modular architecture for future expansion toward exascale quantum dynamics.
summary: The authors present TDSE-Z, a high-performance, open-source framework for simulating strong-field quantum dynamics in materials with position-dependent effective mass. It uses a weak-form Galerkin method on B-splines to solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation. The code is validated by reproducing known physical results, such as WKB decay in quantum wells and HHG spectra, making it a powerful tool for quantum optics and semiconductor physics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of simulating strong-field quantum dynamics in complex materials, particularly those with spatially varying effective mass at interfaces.
main_result: The developed framework, TDSE-Z, successfully implements the BenDaniel-Duke operator using a weak-form Galerkin approach, validating its accuracy across static eigensolvers (WKB comparison) and time propagation (HHG spectra).
method: The core method involves a weak-form Galerkin discretization of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation using B-spline basis functions on geometry-adapted meshes.
model_or_system: The system models atomic, molecular, and semiconductor effective-mass systems, governed by the TDSE incorporating the BenDaniel-Duke kinetic operator, which accounts for spatially varying effective mass m(r).
key_observables: Tunnel splittings, High-Harmonic Generation (HHG) spectra, dipole moment, and total energy expectation values.
important_parameters: Strong laser field amplitudes ($E_0$), dimensionality (1D vs 3D), and the effective mass function $m(r)$.
main_assumptions: The time-propagation engine is currently CPU-optimized, and the framework relies on the weak-form formulation to handle mass-gradient singularities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of 1D vs 3D HHG spectra showing spectral differences due to dimensionality, and plots demonstrate the time evolution of energy and position expectation values confirming numerical stability.
paper_structure: The paper details the implementation of the BDD operator via weak-form Galerkin discretization, validates the static eigensolver against WKB theory, and demonstrates the time-propagation engine on benchmarks like HHG and constant-mass systems.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly robust and general computational tool for simulating light-matter interactions in solid-state and molecular systems, which is central to quantum optics and condensed matter physics.
